title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, documented controls and administrator opt-in default are supported. It accurately warns that exclusions filter web page results only and that news results might still cite excluded sites.

claims.where: front matter: products; title; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap feature concerns domain exclusion for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This feature will allow admins to specify a limited set of sites to exclude from web grounding in M365 Copilot and Copilot Chat #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), not government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-01T23:00:02.
When enabled, web search lets Copilot and Copilot Chat ground responses in public web information.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled, Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat may fetch information from the Bing search service when information from the web helps to provide a better, more grounded response.

claims.claim: Administrators can specify up to 1,000 sites for exclusion from Copilot and Copilot Chat web grounding.
claims.quote: By using domain exclusion, you can specify up to 1,000 sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat through a PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The configuration supports up to two levels of subdomain.
claims.quote: Currently, the domain exclusion configuration supports up to two levels of subdomains.

claims.claim: Tenant domain exclusions are managed with ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1, downloaded from aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.
claims.quote: To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant, use the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 PowerShell script. Download it at https://aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.

claims.claim: The script can get the current configuration and export it to CSV.
claims.quote: Get the current domain exclusion configuration and export to CSV

claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile <csv> creates the tenant domain exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote:
Create your domain exclusion configuration from a CSV file:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile "input.csv"

claims.claim: The script can update an existing domain exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote: Update an existing domain exclusion configuration from CSV file

claims.claim: The script can delete the current domain exclusion configuration.
claims.quote: Delete the current domain exclusion configuration

claims.claim: The script can generate a template CSV for domain exclusions.
claims.quote: Generate a template CSV file for domain exclusions

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Domain exclusion restricts incoming grounding results, currently filtering web page results only.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Other answer verticals, such as news, might still cite excluded sites.
claims.quote: Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.

claims.claim: Domain exclusion is administrator opt-in: the default settings contain no configuration and the administrator runs the script to opt in.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.

claims.claim: Cowork uses the organization's domain exclusion policy.
claims.quote: Cowork uses your organization's domain exclusion policies, including exclusions for specific domains.

claims.claim: The domain exclusion script requires sign-in as Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The script needs the Az.Accounts PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Az.Accounts PowerShell module (the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 script installs the module automatically if it's missing).

claims.claim: An administrator UI for Copilot web-grounding domain exclusions is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "admin center"; Copilot domain exclusion admin center UI. Opened learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion and /copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center; both describe no such UI.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is the Cloud Policy control for web search in both Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The web search policy offers enabled, disabled, and disabled in work mode only options.
claims.quote:
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations can target the tenant's users or specific groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow web search in Copilot" "Graph" API Cloud Policy PowerShell; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "cloud policy" "Copilot" web search. Opened Cloud Policy overview and manage-public-web-access; no corresponding call found.

claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search when Copilot prompt text matches configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The DLP rule condition is Content contains > Sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.claim: The DLP rule action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.

claims.claim: The documented DLP procedure ends by saving and turning on the policy.
claims.quote: Save and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations <location> -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') creates a Copilot DLP policy with the supplied location.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: The policy-creation cmdlet alone does not configure the sensitive-information rule and its web-search action.
claims.quote:
Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.
In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.

claims.claim: Domain-result filtering does not replace the enabled web-search flow that sends generated queries to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: Generated search queries consist of a few words informed by the user's prompt.
claims.quote: This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Generated queries do not include entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote:
The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service:
Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.claim: Generated web search queries can be informed by organizational document content.
claims.quote: Copilot reasons over this document and identifies "clean energy policy" as a major theme. "Clean energy policy" is added to the generated search query sent to the Bing search service (the document itself isn't included).

claims.claim: A generated web search query can contain a manager's name obtained from Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.

claims.claim: A very short prompt can itself be included in the generated query.
claims.quote: The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")

claims.claim: Microsoft presents domain exclusion as part of its layered prompt-injection defenses.
claims.quote: Proactive protections reduce risk by improving visibility, limiting exposure to harmful content, controlling content discovery, and protecting customer data.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented domain-exclusion-specific user messaging at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "user" "message" Copilot. Opened Domain exclusion overview, manage-public-web-access and prompt-defense-in-depth; no domain-exclusion user messaging documented.

claims.claim: Wildcard-style blocking of whole top-level domains is not described for Copilot domain exclusions.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion admin center UI user notification wildcard TLD declarative agents excluded domains; "domain exclusion" wildcard TLD. Opened Domain exclusion overview, including CSV format and limitations; no whole-TLD wildcard syntax.

claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing for domain exclusion is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing meter requirements. Opened Domain exclusion overview, Copilot license options and pay-as-you-go overview; no domain-exclusion-specific licensing rule found.

claims.claim: Feature-specific pricing for domain exclusion is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing meter requirements. Opened Domain exclusion overview, Copilot license options and pay-as-you-go overview; no domain-exclusion-specific price found.

claims.claim: No domain-exclusion meter is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing meter requirements. Opened Domain exclusion overview and Copilot pay-as-you-go overview; billing covers usage of agents and services, with no domain-exclusion meter identified.

claims.claim: Government tenants have web search off by default.
claims.quote: By default, web search is enabled for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat in commercial tenants, but not for U.S. Government Community Cloud (GCC, GCC-High, and DoD) tenants.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can scope web search to specific websites in their manifest.
claims.quote: To scope your web search to specific sites, add the sites property and specify up to four URLs, as shown in the following example.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the interaction between tenant domain exclusions and declarative-agent web search scoped to an excluded site.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "declarative"; Copilot domain exclusion admin center UI user notification wildcard TLD declarative agents excluded domains. Opened Domain exclusion overview and knowledge-sources, Web and scoped web search; no interaction rule found.

claims.claim: The web search control is linked from Copilot > Settings under Data access in the Microsoft 365 admin center, with configuration performed in Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center

claims.claim: Copilot users cannot enable web search with their personal toggle when the administrator policy disables it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.claim: Copilot users retain the option to disable web search with a personal toggle when administrators allow web search.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns on web search for Microsoft Copilot users, those users still have the option to turn off web search by using the Web content toggle.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP policy can apply tenant-wide.
claims.quote: For the entire tenant, use this value: {Type:"Tenant",Identity:"All"}.
